subtitle: Midterm Important Subjective Questions (Solved)
topics: Microbes in Petroleum Industry and Environment

subjective.question: What are the physical factors of the microbial environment?
subjective.answer: The physical factors of the microbial environment are: (1) Temperature, (2) Humidity, (3) pH, and (4) Viscosity.

subjective.question: What are the physiological factors involved in strain production?
subjective.answer: The physiological factors involved in strain production are: (1) Morphology, (2) Metabolic by-products, (3) Shear sensitivity, and (4) Genetic stability of the production strain.

subjective.question: What is bioprocessing of microbes?
subjective.answer: Bioprocessing is the application of natural or genetically manipulated whole cells, tissues or organs, or parts thereof, for the production of industrially or medically important products. It encompasses research, development, manufacturing and commercialization of products prepared by using biological systems. The issues of microorganisms in bioprocessing begin with: Step 1 — isolation of pure or mixed cultures from nature; Step 2 — assessment to determine the capacity for production.

subjective.question: Write the importance of microbial genomics and microbial biotechnology.
subjective.answer: Microbial genomics and microbial biotechnology research is critical for advances in food safety, food security, biotechnology, value-added products, human nutrition and functional foods, plant and animal protection, and for furthering fundamental research in the agricultural sciences. Microbial biotechnology, enabled by genome studies, will lead to breakthroughs such as: improved vaccines and better disease-diagnostic tools; improved microbial agents for biological control of plant and animal pests; modifications of plant and animal pathogens for reduced virulence; development of new industrial catalysts and fermentation organisms; and development of new microbial agents for bioremediation of soil and water contaminated by agricultural runoff.

subjective.question: Why do plants need nitrates?
subjective.answer: Plants need nitrates to make amino acids. Bacteria play an important role in promoting plant growth: they break down dead plants and dead animals by releasing ammonia, which adds nitrogen into the soil. The nitrogen-fixing bacteria in the soil then change the ammonia into nitrates, and these nitrates are used by the plants. Pea and bean plants use the bacterium Rhizobium, which directly converts nitrogen into amino acids.

subjective.question: How do animals digest cellulose?
subjective.answer: One of the main components of plants is cellulose, which is hard for animals to digest. Cellulose can be digested by an enzyme named cellulase. Herbivores depend on bacteria that live in their stomach to digest cellulose: this bacteria secretes cellulase into the stomach, which breaks down the cellulose for the animal.

subjective.question: What is alcoholic fermentation?
subjective.answer: Alcoholic fermentation is done by yeast and certain bacteria. In this process, pyruvate is broken down into alcohol and carbon dioxide. It is used in the production of beer, wine and bread.

subjective.question: What is lactic acid fermentation?
subjective.answer: Lactic acid fermentation occurs in animal muscles when the tissue requires energy at a faster rate than oxygen can be supplied. It is also used to convert lactose into lactic acid in yogurt and cheese production, and it gives the sour taste to fermented vegetables such as pickles.

subjective.question: What is the role of microbes in the meat industry?
subjective.answer: Meat starter cultures are used to make dried, fermented products such as salami, which is a type of cured sausage consisting of fermented and air-dried meat, typically beef or pork; pepperoni, an American variety of salami made from cured pork and beef seasoned with paprika or other chili pepper; and dried ham, which is pork preserved through salting, smoking or wet curing. Lactic bacteria develop the flavour and colour of these products. In addition, a wide variety of moulds are used to ripen the surface of sausages, preserving the natural quality of the product and controlling the development of flavour.

subjective.question: How are microbes important in the dairy industry?
subjective.answer: It would be impossible to make cheese without a starter culture. The production of cheese utilizes starter cultures added to milk with the aim of producing semi-hard and hard cheeses. The starter cultures produce lactic acid, resulting in a pH decrease in the milk and promoting curd synthesis. Yogurt is also a fermented milk product, which takes advantage of lactic-acid-generating Lactobacillus cultures and their use of lactose in milk as a substrate to produce lactic acid; in yogurt and other fermented milk products, the culture is responsible for the taste and texture of the final product. In recent years, probiotic cultures have also become popular in dairy products because of their health benefits.

subjective.question: How are microbes beneficial for the human body?
subjective.answer: In our bodies, different microbes help to digest food, ward off invasive organisms, and engage with the human immune system in the give-and-take of the natural disease process. Probiotic cultures are carefully selected strains, and there is good evidence that they help improve digestion, safeguard the immune system, and keep the body's intestinal flora in balance.

subjective.question: How are microbes used in medicine?
subjective.answer: Some types of microorganisms produce important drugs called antibiotics, whose function is to weaken or destroy other microorganisms. For example, Penicillium notatum is a green mould which produces the antibiotic called penicillin. Some bacteria have also been genetically engineered to produce certain vaccines that are used to prevent infectious diseases, and insulin, which is produced to treat diabetes.

subjective.question: Name two pharmaceutical drugs produced by microbes and describe how they are produced.
subjective.answer: (1) Cyclosporin A: It is used as an immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients and is produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum. (2) Statins: They are produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus and have been commercialised as blood-cholesterol-lowering agents. They act by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible for the synthesis of cholesterol.

subjective.question: What are steroids?
subjective.answer: Steroids are a very important group of chemicals, which are used as anti-inflammatory drugs, and as hormones such as estrogens and progesterone, which are used in oral contraceptives. Producing steroids from animal sources or chemically synthesising them is difficult, but microorganisms can synthesise steroids from sterols or from related compounds.

subjective.question: Name the vitamins produced by microbes.
subjective.answer: Vitamins are organic compounds which are capable of performing many life-sustaining functions inside our body. These compounds cannot be synthesised by humans, and therefore they have to be supplied in small amounts in the diet. Microbes are capable of synthesizing these compounds, and hence they can be used for the commercial production of many of the vitamins, e.g. thiamine (Vitamin B1) and riboflavin (Vitamin B2).

subjective.question: How are microbes economically important?
subjective.answer: Microbes are widely used in large-scale industrial processes, and are used to synthesise a number of products valuable to human beings. This industry has provided products that include beverages, food additives, products for human and animal health, and biofuels. Microbial biotechnology is the application of scientific and engineering principles to the processing of materials by microorganisms to create useful products or processes; the microorganisms utilized may be natural isolates, laboratory-selected mutants, or microbes genetically modified using recombinant DNA methods. It includes the production of antibiotics, organic acids and enzymes by fermentation of microbes.

subjective.question: What are the steps of vaccine production?
subjective.answer: The production of a vaccine can be divided into the following steps: (1) Generation of the antigen — viruses are grown on primary cells such as cells from chicken embryos or fertilised eggs (e.g. influenza vaccine) or on cell lines; bacteria are grown in bioreactors; recombinant proteins are generated in yeast, bacteria or cell cultures. (2) Release and isolation of the antigen — the antigen is separated from the cells and isolated from the proteins and other parts of the growth medium. (3) Purification — the antigen is purified using differences in protein size, physicochemical properties, binding affinity or biological activity. (4) Addition of other components — an adjuvant may be added to enhance the recipient's immune response, along with stabilizers to prolong storage life and preservatives for multi-dose vials. (5) Packaging — the vaccine is filled into vials or syringes, sealed with sterile stoppers, labelled and distributed, following Good Manufacturing Practices.

subjective.question: What are DNA vaccines? Give an example.
subjective.answer: DNA vaccines are still in the experimental stage and show great promise. These vaccines take immunization to a new technological level: they dispense with both the whole organism and its parts, and get right down to the essentials — the microbe's genetic material — which then triggers the immune response. Example: influenza vaccine.

subjective.question: Define a live attenuated vaccine and give an example.
subjective.answer: A live attenuated vaccine is a vaccine prepared from live microorganisms (bacteria or viruses) that have been weakened (attenuated) in the laboratory so that they have lost their disease-causing ability (virulence), but can still multiply in the body and produce a strong, long-lasting immune response without causing the disease. Example: the BCG vaccine used against tuberculosis.

subjective.topic: Microbes in Petroleum Industry and Environment
subjective.question: Define biosurfactants and explain their role in bioremediation.
subjective.answer: Biosurfactants are microbial-synthesized surface-active substances that allow for more efficient microbial biodegradation of hydrocarbons in bioremediation processes. There are two ways by which biosurfactants are involved in bioremediation: (1) They increase the surface area of hydrophobic water-insoluble substrates — growth of microbes on hydrocarbons can be limited by the available surface area of the water-oil interface, and emulsifiers produced by microbes can break up oil into smaller droplets, effectively increasing the available surface area. (2) They increase the bioavailability of hydrophobic water-insoluble substrates by desorbing them from surfaces (e.g. soil) or by increasing their apparent solubility; some biosurfactants have low critical micelle concentrations (CMCs), which increases the apparent solubility of hydrocarbons by sequestering hydrophobic molecules into the centres of micelles.

subjective.topic: Microbes in Petroleum Industry and Environment
subjective.question: What is Microbial Enhanced Oil Recovery (MEOR)?
subjective.answer: One of the major concerns facing the oil industry today is the recovery of the large percentage of oil remaining unrecovered in mature and nearly depleted oil fields. In Microbial Enhanced Oil Recovery (MEOR), microbes influence and improve the oil recovery process by: generating gases that increase reservoir pressure and decrease oil viscosity; generating acids that dissolve rock, thus improving absolute permeability; reducing permeability in channels; producing biosurfactants that decrease interfacial tension; and reducing oil viscosity by degrading long-chain saturated hydrocarbons.

subjective.topic: Microbes in Petroleum Industry and Environment
subjective.question: What is a biofuel? How are biofuels obtained?
subjective.answer: A biofuel is a fuel that is produced through contemporary biological processes, such as agriculture and anaerobic digestion, rather than a fuel produced by geological processes such as those involved in the formation of fossil fuels like coal and petroleum. Biofuels are obtained when modified enzymes and microorganisms turn abundant biomass into feedstocks: organic solvents such as ethanol, acetone, butanol and glycerol can be commercially produced by using microbes and low-cost raw materials (e.g. wood, cellulose and starch).

subjective.topic: Microbes in Petroleum Industry and Environment
subjective.question: What are biopesticides? Write their advantages.
subjective.answer: Biopesticides are pesticides derived from natural materials such as microorganisms, plants and other biological sources, used to control pests by biological means. Their advantages are: they are eco-friendly and biodegradable, so they do not pollute soil and water; they are target-specific and do not harm beneficial organisms, humans or animals; they leave no toxic chemical residues on food crops; and pests develop resistance against them much more slowly than against chemical pesticides.

subjective.topic: Microbes in Petroleum Industry and Environment
subjective.question: Define compost and write its types.
subjective.answer: Compost is the dark, nutrient-rich, humus-like organic material obtained by the controlled decomposition of organic wastes (such as food scraps, leaves and manure) by microorganisms; it is used as a fertilizer and soil amendment. Its main types are: (1) Hot composting — rapid aerobic decomposition in a turned, aerated heap; (2) Cold composting — slow decomposition of organic matter piled without regular turning; and (3) Worm composting (vermicomposting) — using worms to recycle food scraps and other organic material into a valuable soil amendment called vermicompost, or worm compost.

subjective.topic: Microbes in Petroleum Industry and Environment
subjective.question: How is soil treatment carried out with biofertilizers and compost?
subjective.answer: In soil treatment, all the biofertilizers along with the compost fertilizers are mixed together and kept for one night. The next day, the mixture is spread on the soil where seeds have to be sown, so that the beneficial microbes establish themselves in the soil and support plant growth.
